page.headline: Smart home device onboarding
start.manual_body: Pick manufacturer, model and connection step by step.
start.qr_body: Recognize a device by QR code or product code.
step.category.title: What do you want to set up?
step.category.body: Start by choosing the kind of device. Smart Guide then asks for manufacturer, model, connection and requirements.
step.manufacturer.title: Which manufacturer?
step.manufacturer.body: The manufacturer often decides whether you need a local integration, a bridge or a cloud connection.
step.model.title: Which model?
step.model.body: The model narrows down the right integration path. If you're not sure, pick the closest match.
step.connection.title: Which connection does it use?
step.connection.body: The radio or network type determines which infrastructure has to be in place before the actual setup.
step.infrastructure.title: Automatic requirements check
step.infrastructure.body: Smart Guide first checks what it can find out from Home Assistant. Only unclear points are asked.
step.result.title: Assessment and integration path
step.result.body: Smart Guide shows whether the path works, which requirements are missing and what to do next.
wizard.no_devices_for_vendor: No devices found for this manufacturer.
wizard.too_many_devices: {count} devices found. Refine the search to narrow down the list.
infra.wifi.same_network.label: Device is on the same network as Home Assistant
infra.wifi.same_network.question: Can Home Assistant reach the device on the same network?
infra.wifi.same_network.action: Connect the device to the same Wi-Fi/LAN or check VLAN and firewall rules.
infra.wifi.local_integration.label: A Home Assistant integration or local API is available
infra.wifi.local_integration.question: Is there a Home Assistant integration for this manufacturer or device?
infra.wifi.local_integration.action: Check Devices & Services in Home Assistant first, then the official integration list.
infra.wifi.cloud_dependency.label: Cloud dependency has been checked
infra.wifi.cloud_dependency.question: Can the device be controlled locally, or does it need a manufacturer cloud?
infra.wifi.cloud_dependency.action: If only cloud control is possible, mark the path as cloud-dependent or choose a device that integrates locally.
infra.zigbee.zigbee_stack.label: Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA is installed
infra.zigbee.zigbee_stack.question: Is ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT available in Home Assistant?
infra.zigbee.zigbee_stack.action: Install ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT before adding a Zigbee device.
infra.zigbee.zigbee_coordinator.label: Zigbee coordinator is connected
infra.zigbee.zigbee_coordinator.question: Is a Zigbee coordinator plugged in and online?
infra.zigbee.zigbee_coordinator.action: Additional hardware required: connect a Zigbee coordinator and set it up in Home Assistant.
infra.zigbee.mqtt.label: MQTT is configured (for Zigbee2MQTT)
infra.zigbee.mqtt.question: Is MQTT configured for Zigbee2MQTT?
infra.zigbee.mqtt.action: Install or configure an MQTT broker if you want to use Zigbee2MQTT.
infra.matter.matter_server.label: Matter server add-on or integration is available
infra.matter.matter_server.question: Is Matter set up in Home Assistant?
infra.matter.matter_server.action: Set up the Matter server add-on or the Matter integration.
infra.matter.thread_router.label: A Thread border router is available (for Thread devices)
infra.matter.thread_router.question: Is there a Thread border router for Thread devices?
infra.matter.thread_router.action: Additional hardware required if the Matter device uses Thread instead of Wi-Fi.
infra.matter.same_network.label: Device and Home Assistant are on the same network
infra.matter.same_network.question: Can the device and Home Assistant reach each other on the same network?
infra.matter.same_network.action: Check network, VLAN, mDNS and firewall.
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_adapter.label: A Bluetooth adapter or proxy is available
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_adapter.questi: Is Bluetooth or a Bluetooth proxy available in Home Assistant?
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_adapter.action: Enable a Bluetooth adapter or deploy an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy.
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_range.label: The device is within range
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_range.question: Is the device reliably within Bluetooth range?
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_range.action: Place a Bluetooth proxy closer to the device or switch to Zigbee/Matter/Wi-Fi.
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_integration.la: The Home Assistant Bluetooth integration is active
infra.bluetooth.bluetooth_integration.ac: Enable the Bluetooth integration in Home Assistant.
infra.lan.known_ip.label: Device has a fixed or discoverable IP address
infra.lan.known_ip.question: Is the device's IP address or network discovery known?
infra.lan.known_ip.action: Look it up in your router, assign a fixed IP or check network discovery.
infra.lan.local_control.label: Local control is enabled
infra.lan.local_control.question: Is local control or a local API enabled?
infra.lan.local_control.action: Enable local control in the manufacturer app or the device's web interface.
infra.lan.firewall.label: Firewall does not block Home Assistant
infra.lan.firewall.question: Can Home Assistant reach the device on the network?
infra.lan.firewall.action: Check firewall, VLAN and mDNS rules.
infra.bridge.bridge_reachable.label: Bridge is reachable on the network
infra.bridge.bridge_reachable.question: Is the manufacturer bridge reachable on the network?
infra.bridge.bridge_reachable.action: Power on the bridge, check the network and assign a fixed IP if needed.
infra.bridge.bridge_paired.label: Device is already paired with the bridge
infra.bridge.bridge_paired.question: Is the device already paired with the bridge?
infra.bridge.bridge_paired.action: Pair the device with the manufacturer bridge first.
infra.bridge.bridge_integration.label: The matching Home Assistant integration is installed
infra.bridge.bridge_integration.question: Is the matching bridge integration available in Home Assistant?
infra.bridge.bridge_integration.action: Set up the bridge integration in Home Assistant; the devices will show up afterwards.
recommendation.wifi: First check whether Home Assistant can discover the device locally. If only a cloud integration exists, the recommendation should be clearly marked as cloud-dependent.
recommendation.zigbee: The next sensible step is choosing between ZHA and Zigbee2MQTT. Don't start pairing devices without a coordinator and, for Zigbee2MQTT, an MQTT broker.
recommendation.matter: Matter is a good fit once the Matter infrastructure is in place. For Thread devices, the border router is the key requirement.
recommendation.bluetooth: Bluetooth suits nearby devices or setups with Bluetooth proxies. Without stable range, Wi-Fi, Zigbee or Matter is often more robust.
recommendation.lan: LAN is usually the most stable local path. What matters is whether the manufacturer offers a local integration or a documented API.
recommendation.bridge: The bridge handles pairing and the radio network. Add the bridge to Home Assistant first; individual devices show up after that.
error.managed_connection: The Home Assistant connection is managed by the add-on.
analysis.next.check_foundations: The main device capabilities have been detected. For new devices, Smart Guide should next clarify whether Zigbee, MQTT, Matter or Thread is available.
analysis.next.choose_device: Now choose which new device you want to add. Smart Guide uses the detected capabilities as context.
analysis.next.manual_start: Start with the manual device selection. Smart Guide then checks which integration path makes sense.

pairing.title: Connect Zigbee device
pairing.subtitle: Smart Guide now walks you through pairing and discovery.
pairing.step1_title: 1. Put the device in pairing mode
pairing.step1_body: Put the device into pairing mode now.
pairing.instruction_ts011f: On many TS011F plugs, hold the button for about 5-10 seconds until the LED blinks rapidly.
pairing.instruction_generic: Usually: hold the reset button for 5-10 seconds until the LED blinks.
pairing.step2_body: Smart Guide starts pairing mode or tells you clearly what's still missing.
pairing.step3_body: Smart Guide then checks whether Home Assistant reports a new device.
pairing.ready_message: Good. Now start discovery in Home Assistant.
pairing.hint_closer: Move the device closer to the coordinator
pairing.hint_logs: Check the Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA logs

pairing.api.not_connected_message: Automatic pairing mode is prepared, but Home Assistant is not connected yet.
pairing.api.unreachable_message: Pairing mode could not be started, Home Assistant is currently unreachable.
pairing.api.coordinator_timeout_error: Zigbee coordinator did not respond in time
pairing.api.coordinator_timeout_message: The pairing command was sent to Zigbee2MQTT, but the Zigbee coordinator did not confirm within a few seconds that pairing mode is active. This points to a coordinator/firmware problem, not a Smart Guide problem — check the Zigbee2MQTT logs on the host.
pairing.api.no_stack_error: No Zigbee coordinator (ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT) detected.
pairing.api.no_stack_message: Smart Guide is connected to Home Assistant but finds neither ZHA nor Zigbee2MQTT there, so pairing mode can't be started automatically.
pairing.api.service_rejected: Home Assistant rejected the service call (HTTP {code})
pairing.api.start_failed: Pairing mode could not be started.
pairing.api.started: Pairing mode started via {backend} for {duration} seconds.
pairing.api.no_baseline: Pairing mode has not been started yet, so there's no baseline to compare new devices against.
pairing.api.nothing_new: No new device found yet. Home Assistant hasn't reported a new entity in these domains since pairing started.
pairing.api.found.one: {count} new entity found since pairing started.
pairing.api.found.other: {count} new entities found since pairing started.
